title: 測量実習・演習Ⅱ
subtitle: Surveying Practicum / Exercises II
keywords: Distance, Degree, Bearing 2.Error, Precision 3.Control Point Surveying 4.Digital Photogrammetry,GNSS Survey
educationalGoal: (1) Students will practice the surveying methods learned in Surveying I and Surveying II(2) Students will practice control point surveying, digital photogrammetry and GNSS surveying (3) Students will prepare reports that are equivalent professional company reports and will learn how to create data and reports.
advice: Surveying practice will be undertaken as active learning based on “Total Ability” learning in the CLIP learning process. (1) Traverse Surveying Students will gain practical knowledge about traverse surveying as an application of control point surveying learned in Surveying II (2) GNSS surveying Students will practice real-time positioning using a network-based RTK method and static positioning using VRS-GPS. (3) Digital Photogrammetry Students will learn digital photogrammetry practices using “Image Master Beginners” developed by the JSPRS (Japan Society of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing) and Topcon Ltd.
requiredKnowledge: In Surveying Practicum II, students strengthen their understanding of the contents learned in Surveying I and II with practical skills. Students must fully understand the content from the classroom lectures in Surveying I and II. Spatial information engineering is offered as a related high-level class and other surveying-related courses include environmental Civil Engineering Experiments B and Exercises in Geoinformatics.

activityGoals.body: Students can operate Total Station measurements and explain the basics of GNSS surveying. (0.1L,0.1M)
Students can understand surveying methods depending on the survey needs.(0.1L,0.1M)
Students will deepen their insight into specific planning.(0.1L,0.1M)
Students can acquire literacy in goematics processing, including photogrammetry, GNSS, and GIS.(0.1H,0.1L)
Students acquire the basic skills of engineers, the basic skills of specialists.(0.2M)

achievementLevels.ideal: Students can achieve accuracies of over 1/5000 with high closing ratios in traverse surveying, and can carry out precise calculation processing.Students set up the tripod in less than 3 minutes. Students show a very high level of engineering consideration in their writing about the practice of GNSS positioning. Students show a very high level of engineering consideration in their writing about the practice of digital photogrammetry.
achievementLevels.standard: Students can achieve accuracies of over 1/3000 with high closing ratios in traverse surveying, and can carry out calculation processing. Students can write about the engineering considerations of GNSS. Students can write about the engineering considerations of digital photogrammetry.
